title: Absolute Gysin purity on regular affine schemes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work on the small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of Noetherian regular affine schemes [def-weil-regular-scheme], with $\ell$ invertible. Such an $f$ admits a factorization into a regular closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; regular means that the ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The difference between the smooth relative dimension and the length of that sequence is the locally constant virtual relative dimension $d_f$ on $Y$. The etale exceptional right adjoint $f_n^!$ of compact support $Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] has a canonical Gysin isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{f,n}:\Lambda_{n,Y}(d_f)[2d_f]\xrightarrow{\sim}f_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}.$$
These Gysin maps are independent of the factorization and compatible with composition under exceptional-pullback transitivity, with the identity morphism, and with etale base change and localization (also strict localization, by continuity). For a closed immersion of codimension $c$ one has $d_f=-c$. For a quasi-finite $f$, at any $y\in Y$ one has $d_f(y)=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}-\dim\mathcal O_{X,f(y)}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; quasi-finite here means finite type with finite fibres. For every coefficient quotient $\Lambda_N\to\Lambda_n$ with $N\geq n$, the coefficient map on the source of $\operatorname{Cl}_{f,N}$ followed by $\operatorname{Cl}_{f,n}$ equals the map obtained by applying coefficient change to the Gysin class. On twists this coefficient map is induced by $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ on roots of unity.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 2.3.1, Theorem 2.3.2, Definitions 2.5.3 and 2.5.11, Theorem 2.5.12, Theorem 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2; coefficient diagrams in section 3.3, Propositions 3.3.1–3.3.2; XVII Lemma 2.4.3.4 (regular affine quasi-finite case).

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The finite-type affine presentation embeds $Y$ in $\mathbf A_X^r$. By [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] this is a regular closed immersion and the intermediate scheme is regular. The same input gives the intrinsic, locally constant integer $d_f=r-c$, and shows that every other smooth/regular factorization has this same integer. All maps between the affine schemes used below are separated and finite type; [thm-nagata-compactification] makes them compactifiable and [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies their ordinary etale right adjoints. Work componentwise when dimensions vary. No excellence or field hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: XVI Definitions 2.5.1–2.5.3 and paragraph after Definition 2.5.2; regular affine case of Corollary 3.1.2

proof.text:
For $a$ of virtual dimension $d_a$, put $a^?=a_n^!(-d_a)[-2d_a]$. Exceptional composition is the mate of associative compact-support composition [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] followed by the open tensor formula [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] gives the projection formula for a compactification. For an invertible Tate line $L$, adjunction and its tensor inverse give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,a^!(K\otimes L))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!M,K\otimes L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!(M\otimes a^*L^{-1}),K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,a^!K\otimes a^*L).$$
Yoneda gives the required twist commutation, with the pulled-back line identified by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For $b$ after $a$ and normalized classes $v:\Lambda\to b^?\Lambda$, $u:\Lambda\to a^?\Lambda$, set $v\star u=a^?(v)\circ u$. Both bracketings of three classes equal $a^?b^?(w)\circ a^?(v)\circ u$, by functoriality and the associative composition comparisons.

For $f=pi$ take the supported Kummer map $a_i:\Lambda\to i^?\Lambda$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] and the shifted diagonal/DNC smooth orientation $a_p:\Lambda\to p^?\Lambda$ of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. Define $a_{p,i}=a_p\star a_i$. Undoing the normalizing twist gives $\operatorname{Cl}_{p,i}:\Lambda_Y(r-c)[2(r-c)]\to f_n^!\Lambda_X$. The immersion in step 1 is a regular pair, so [lem-per-gabber-regular-pair-purity] makes $a_i$ invertible; smooth purity makes $a_p$ invertible. A functor takes an inverse to an inverse, so their composite is an isomorphism.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.5.4 and Theorem 3.1.1; smooth normalization from Scholze Theorem 7.19

proof.text:
First compare factorizations $f=pi=p'i'$ equipped with a smooth map $q:P'\to P$ satisfying $qi'=i$ and $pq=p'$. Form $T=Y\times_P P'$ with projections $j:T\hookrightarrow P'$ and $q':T\to Y$. The map $s=(1_Y,i'):Y\to T$ is a closed section of $q'$ and $js=i'$. Smooth base change and regular-immersion geometry [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] make $j,s$ regular; all schemes here are regular. The two identities of [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities] give $a_q\star a_j=a_i\star a_{q'}$ and $a_{q'}\star a_s=1$. Regular-immersion composition [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] gives $a_{i'}=a_j\star a_s$. Therefore
$$a_q\star a_{i'}=(a_i\star a_{q'})\star a_s=a_i.$$
Smooth composition [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] now gives $a_{p',i'}=a_p\star a_q\star a_{i'}=a_{p,i}$.

source.place: XVI Theorem 2.5.5, proof after Definition 2.5.6 and Lemmas 2.5.7–2.5.8

proof.text: First take separated smooth factorizations $Y\hookrightarrow P\to X$ and $Y\hookrightarrow P'\to X$. Use $Q=P\times_XP'$ and $k=(i,i'):Y\hookrightarrow Q$. Both projections are smooth. The map $k$ is closed: its graph into $Y\times_XP'$ is closed since $P'/X$ is separated, and the next map is the base change of $i$. Locally on affine rings the composite map to $B$ is surjective since the $P$ factor already surjects. The scheme $Q$ is regular, being smooth over regular $P$, so $k$ is regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. Step 4 applied to both projections identifies the two classes. Their common value $a_f$ equals the isomorphism of step 3. If a smooth intermediate scheme is not separated, compute its class on affine neighbourhoods of the image of each point of $Y$; these are separated over affine $X$. Exceptional locality [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies the restricted targets. These local classes agree with the restriction of the affine-space class by the separated comparison just proved. They therefore define that same global class. Equality can be tested locally here: step 3 identifies the target with the source invertible Tate line with its shift, whose degree-zero endomorphisms are sections of $\Lambda_Y$. Thus no separatedness hypothesis on a chosen smooth factorization is silently imposed.

source.place: XVI Theorem 2.5.5, first reduction to a common smooth refinement

proof.text:
Let $Y\xrightarrow fX\xrightarrow gS$ be composable maps as in the statement. Choose $X\xrightarrow jV\xrightarrow vS$ for $g$ and $Y\xrightarrow i\mathbf A_X^r\xrightarrow pX$ for $f$. Put $V'=\mathbf A_V^r$ with projection $p':V'\to V$ and the base-changed regular immersion $j':\mathbf A_X^r\hookrightarrow V'$. The common composite factors as $gf=vp'j'i$. All intermediate schemes are regular; [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] gives regularity and codimension additivity, so its virtual dimension is $d_f+f^*d_g$. Regular-immersion composition, smooth composition and the mixed square identity give, respectively,
$$a_{j'i}=a_{j'}\star a_i,\quad a_{vp'}=a_v\star a_{p'},\quad a_{p'}\star a_{j'}=a_j\star a_p.$$
Thus $a_{gf}=a_v\star a_{p'}\star a_{j'}\star a_i=(a_v\star a_j)\star(a_p\star a_i)=a_g\star a_f$. Factorization independence from step 5 makes this the claimed exceptional-transitivity formula for every choice. Undo the twist normalization to obtain the formula for $\operatorname{Cl}_{f,n}$.

source.place: XVI Theorem 2.5.12, proof using affine space instead of projective space

proof.text:
The identity factorization has regular codimension zero and smooth dimension zero. Its two classes are identities by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus, lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality], so $\operatorname{Cl}_{1,n}=1$. For a closed immersion use the immersion itself followed by the identity: $d_f=0-c=-c$ and its class is the shifted regular-immersion class. For quasi-finite $f$, [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] says the residue extension is finite and the intrinsic formula is
$$d_f(y)=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}-\dim\mathcal O_{X,f(y)}+0,$$
which is the asserted equality.

source.place: XVI Definitions 2.3.1 and 2.5.1; XVII Lemma 2.4.3.4, dimension equality

proof.text: After an etale change of base or an open restriction, pull back an affine-space factorization of $f$. Its immersion remains regular with the same codimension [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. The supported Kummer class and the diagonal/DNC smooth orientation restrict to the corresponding classes by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus, lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. Their composite therefore restricts to the class of the pulled-back factorization, hence to $\operatorname{Cl}_{f',n}$ by step 5. The exceptional comparison here is the canonical etale-local comparison, not a claim of arbitrary exceptional base change for a nonsmooth map. To identify the exceptional targets, take mates of compact-support base change [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]; etale sum extension is left adjoint to etale pullback [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], so adjunction and compact-support composition identify the two right adjoints. This identifies the comparison used for the two classes.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.3.1 and Proposition 2.2.3.1; etale localization of the construction in Definition 2.5.4

proof.text: For localization or strict localization, restrict the same chosen factorization along the affine ind-etale system of neighbourhoods defining the local or strict-local scheme. The regular-immersion supported class has the localization and continuity property stated in [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. The smooth map and its orientation pull back to the Noetherian local or strict-local base by [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. These give the two factors of the restricted class, so their composite is the local class. This also specifies what localization compatibility means when a local-scheme map itself is not finite type: the exceptional comparison and class are those induced by restricting the fixed finite-type factorization, not an additional compact-support functor for the localization map.

source.place: XVI section 3.2 before Definition 3.2.2; restriction of Definition 2.5.4 and supported continuity

proof.text: Keep one geometric factorization for $\Lambda_N$ and $\Lambda_n$. Reduction sends its supported Kummer class to the level-$n$ class [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] and sends its diagonal/DNC smooth orientation to the level-$n$ orientation [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. The coefficient comparison is defined by the compact-support counit; its compatibility with composition and tensor follows from the actual compact-support scalar identities in [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] by taking adjoint transposes. Hence reduction of $a_p\star a_i$ is the composite of the two reduced classes, namely $a_{p,n}\star a_{i,n}=a_{f,n}$. The Tate transition is $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; dual tensor comparisons give signed twists. This proves equality of the specified maps, rather than just the existence of isomorphic objects after reduction. The case $N=n$ is the identity, and composing two power transitions multiplies their exponents, as required for successive quotients. Its composition assertion applies here: after the purity isomorphisms of step 3, all coefficient objects involved are shifted invertible Tate lines, hence are bounded below and remain so under derived coefficient reduction. No bounded-below assertion for the reduction of an arbitrary complex is used.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.3.1 coefficient square and Proposition 3.3.2 compatible representatives; diagonal/DNC normalization for the smooth factor

split_report.summary: Split by the smooth/regular factorization argument, writing the common-refinement and composition calculations in the item. Five statement-only inputs isolate intrinsic geometry, supported regular classes, Gabber regular-pair purity, general-Noetherian prime-power diagonal smooth purity, and the two mixed smooth/immersion identities. Retained all hypotheses and all coefficient/localization clauses; no SGA trace input. No exact Lean or Mathlib attachment found. On resumption, restored the Mathlib records from the saved, logged command outputs (including the item query), replaced an invalid Loogle query by an additional valid query, and checked the bounded-below condition of scalar-composition coherence on the actual invertible coefficient objects.
